title: the cord that binds us: practicing devotion
content:
artifacts are metaphorical-poetic teachings for navigating the creative life, released as a part of labyrinth library.

explore this artifact

I made this artifact as a way into thinking about devotion - the nature and quality of our devotion, visualized as cosmic cords that bind us — in relation to those things we love, or feel obligated to. this could be anything: our creative practices, our businesses, the relationships and ties that keep us anchored in our lives.

sometimes love, too, can feel like obligation, like a burden. sometimes we run away from our own devotion, because it comes layered with “shoulds,” or the internalized expectations of others.

but, there are many ways of being devoted. devotion doesn’t have to be a singular thing, measured in daily prostrations or a constant, centripetal orbit around the object of one’s devotion. cords are meant to stretch, tangle, break, and form again.

we can learn how to be elastic in our devotion. we can offer devotion even in the midst of confusion and grief; the bond will just need to take a different shape. it takes care and presence to even begin to discover - with tenderness and curiosity - what the shape of our true devotion might look like, lived in the tactile, day to day of our lives.


*
purpose — to bring attention to the cords that bind you in relationship — to your creative practices, visions, dreams, desires, or to the people and places in your life.

guiding question — what are the cords that bind you, and what is the quality of the bond?
